questions.question: [Test 25 - Q1] The 'Project Method' of teaching, which focuses on solving real-world, purposeful problems in a social environment, was developed by:
questions.explanation: Kilpatrick formulated the Project Method based on pragmatism and the educational philosophies of his mentor, John Dewey. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q2] The 'Heuristic Method' of teaching, which places the student in the role of an active discoverer or researcher, was pioneered by:
questions.explanation: H. E. Armstrong developed the Heuristic Method (from the Greek 'heuriskein' meaning 'to discover') to foster scientific enquiry and self-learning. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q3] Who developed the linear model of 'Programmed Instruction', which breaks down learning material into small steps called 'frames' with immediate feedback?
questions.explanation: B. F. Skinner developed linear programmed instruction based on operant conditioning, whereas Norman Crowder developed branching programmed instruction. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q4] Which quantitative method, developed by Jacob L. Moreno, is used to measure and map social relations, attractions, and repulsions within a classroom or group?
questions.explanation: Sociometry is a tool used to visually map and analyze social structures, peer acceptance, and interpersonal relationships within a classroom. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q5] The classic formula for calculating the Intelligence Quotient (IQ), (Mental Age / Chronological Age) * 100, was first formulated by:
questions.explanation: William Stern of Germany first proposed the concept of IQ and its formula in 1912, which was subsequently adapted and popularized by Lewis Terman in the Stanford-Binet intelligence scale. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q6] According to National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, what is the new pedagogical and curricular structure replacing the existing 10+2 structure in Indian school education?
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 replaces the traditional 10+2 system with a 5+3+3+4 structure corresponding to Foundational (5 yrs), Preparatory (3 yrs), Middle (3 yrs), and Secondary (4 yrs) stages. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q7] Which of the following principles best characterizes Jean Piaget's theory of cognitive development regarding the process of Schema Adaptation?
questions.explanation: Piaget defined adaptation as the balance achieved through assimilation (incorporating new info into existing schemas) and accommodation (modifying existing schemas to fit new info). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q8] In Lev Vygotsky's Socio-Cultural Theory, the term 'Scaffolding' refers to:
options: Temporary support given by a More Knowledgeable Other (MKO) during the learning process
Permanent structural changes in cognitive architecture
Rote memorization techniques for complex concepts
Standardized testing procedures in formative assessment
questions.explanation: Scaffolding is a supportive framework provided by a teacher or peer (MKO) within the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) that is gradually removed as the learner gains independence. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q9] Under the Right to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009, what is the mandatory Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) prescribed for primary schools (Classes I to V)?
questions.explanation: As per the RTE Act 2009, the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) for primary schools (Classes 1-5) is mandated at 30:1 for enrollment up to 200 students. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q10] Formative Assessment is primarily aimed at which of the following instructional goals?
options: Providing ongoing feedback to improve learning and teaching during the instructional process
Assigning final grades at the end of an academic semester
Ranking students based on normative curve distribution
questions.explanation: Formative assessment is 'Assessment FOR Learning' designed to monitor student learning and provide continuous feedback to teachers and students to modify teaching-learning activities. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q11] In Bloom's Revised Taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001), which level represents the highest order of cognitive processing?
questions.explanation: In Anderson & Krathwohl's revised taxonomy (2001), 'Creating' (generating new ideas or products) replaced 'Evaluation' at the highest cognitive level. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q12] Which teaching model is based on Jerome Bruner's concept of Discovery Learning and Enactive-Iconic-Symbolic modes of representation?
questions.explanation: Bruner proposed constructivist discovery learning where learners build knowledge through enactive (action-based), iconic (image-based), and symbolic (language-based) modes. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q13] Inclusive Education in Indian classrooms fundamentally implies:
options: Educating children with special needs alongside non-disabled children in regular classrooms with appropriate adaptations
Establishing separate special schools for children with disabilities
Admitting only high-achieving gifted students in mainstream schools
Providing home-based schooling for all children with mild learning difficulties
questions.explanation: Inclusive education ensures that all children, regardless of their physical, cognitive, social, or linguistic abilities, learn together in the same mainstream educational environment. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q14] In Howard Gardner's Theory of Multiple Intelligences, a person with high ability to perceive and understand others' moods, motivations, and feelings possesses high:
questions.explanation: Interpersonal intelligence involves understanding and interacting effectively with others, whereas Intrapersonal intelligence involves self-awareness and self-understanding. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q15] What is the primary objective of Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE)?
options: To evaluate all aspects of student development, including scholastic and co-scholastic domains continuously
To conduct quarterly written examinations to eliminate low performers
To substitute internal assessments with final external board examinations
To reduce teacher workload by automating grading systems
questions.explanation: CCE evaluates both scholastic (academic) and co-scholastic (life skills, attitudes, values) growth of a learner continuously throughout the academic cycle. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q16] According to Lawrence Kohlberg's theory of Moral Development, an individual who obeys rules solely to avoid punishment is at which stage?
options: Pre-conventional Level (Stage 1: Punishment and Obedience Orientation)
Conventional Level (Stage 3: Good Boy-Nice Girl Orientation)
Conventional Level (Stage 4: Law and Order Orientation)
questions.explanation: Stage 1 of Kohlberg's Pre-conventional level is characterized by obedience driven by fear of physical punishment or deference to superior power. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q17] Which of the following best describes the concept of 'Diagnostic Teaching' in pedagogy?
options: Identifying specific learning difficulties and gaps in students to plan targeted remedial instruction
Conducting annual medical checkups for students in government schools
Sorting students into homogenous sections based on IQ scores
Delivering lectures without asking questions to test retention
questions.explanation: Diagnostic assessment identifies specific areas of weakness or misconceptions, serving as the basis for remedial teaching strategies. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q18] In Carl Rogers' Humanistic Theory of Education, the role of the teacher is primarily envisioned as a:
questions.explanation: Rogers emphasized person-centered education where the teacher acts as a facilitator providing an empathetic, authentic, and accepting environment for self-directed learning. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q19] Which of the following is an example of an 'Intrinsic Motivation' factor in student learning?
options: Inherent curiosity and personal satisfaction derived from mastering a subject
Receiving cash prizes and gold medals from the school principal
Avoidance of parental disapproval or detention after school
Desire to secure first position in class merit list
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation arises from internal rewards—such as curiosity, interest, personal enjoyment, or autonomy—rather than external incentives or punishments. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).

questions.question: [Test 25 - Q20] Action Research in classroom pedagogy is defined as:
options: A reflective process conducted by teachers to solve immediate practical problems in their own classroom
Pure theoretical research conducted by university professors
Nationwide statistical survey on school enrollment ratios
Historical analysis of ancient educational systems
questions.explanation: Action research is practitioner-based inquiry aimed at diagnosing and solving specific classroom problems to enhance pedagogical effectiveness. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 25).
